newsitem.title: GERMANY: Weather holds key to July/Aug oilseeds prices.
newsitem.headline: Weather holds key to July/Aug oilseeds prices.

text.p: Global oilseeds prices in July and August were in the hands of crop weather trends, with favourable weather appearing to continue in United States soybeans areas, the independent newsletter Oil World said.
While this could bring downward pressure over the next week or two, Oil World believed soybean prices had already been near their fundamentally justified lows on July 1-3.
Further ahead, the publication stressed North American crop weather could deteriorate during the next two to three months.
While noting the U.S. Agriculture Department had raised a soybean area estimate on June 30 by two million acres to 70.9 million acres, it said this could be overriden by yield losses.
"...even slightly adverse weather would more than offset the advantage of two million more acres," it said.
World crop weather trends in June were mostly favourable in the U.S., Europe, and the former USSR, and mixed in China, India and the Philippines, Oil World noted.
But Malaysia and Australia were under threat of drought arising from the El Nino pattern and this was expected to last.
Elsewhere, growers in the Philippines were fearing dry conditions in major coconut regions and Indian farmers were complaining about the uneven distribution of monsoon rains.
